sections.h2: Choosing how to sell in Augusta
sections.html:
A seller here can go the agent route, handle the sale privately, or let a cash buyer take the house untouched. Condition, calendar and the price cut you will accept for certainty usually settle the choice.

  • Agent route: the broadest exposure, with inspection haggling and a lender's schedule attached.
  • Private sale: the listing fee stays with you, and so does every chore.
  • Cash buyer: the fewest moving parts, with an offer shaped by the buyer's own repair and resale costs.

Whichever you pick, the assessment calendar, the local exemption and Georgia's transfer tax all apply, and each gets its own section below.

sections.h2: One government for city and county
sections.html:
The City of Augusta and Richmond County merged in 1996, and Augusta-Richmond County is one of only three consolidated governments in Georgia. A mayor and ten commissioners run it, and Hephzibah and Blythe stay independent inside the county lines. If your address is in one of them, ask which city charges also appear on your bill. In practice, one set of offices handles every parcel, so ask the tax commissioner what charges appear on yours.

Augusta is about 150 miles east of Atlanta along Interstate 20, and the Savannah River marks the border with Aiken County, South Carolina. Nine of its neighborhoods are on the federal historic register, and old neighborhoods mean old houses. If yours stands in a designated historic district, ask the city's preservation commission which exterior changes need approval before you pay for a pre-sale refresh.

Soldiers, doctors and students supply much of the local demand. Fort Eisenhower (formerly Fort Gordon), NSA Augusta and the Savannah River Site anchor a cybersecurity and advanced operations cluster.

  • Medical District: Augusta University Health, Piedmont Augusta and the Charlie Norwood VA.
  • Colleges: Augusta University, Augusta Technical College and Paine College.
  • Tournament week: the Masters is played during the first full week of April, and many owners rent their houses out for it.

Postings change on a fixed calendar. An owner who gets orders, or inherits a house from a relative stationed elsewhere, may have a short runway before mortgage and vacant-house costs add up.

Augusta-Richmond County had an estimated 201,999 people in mid-2025, barely changed from 202,081 in the 2020 census. Renting and owning split almost evenly, so landlords and tenants carry real weight in local sales.

sections.h2: Assessment notices and the appeal clock
sections.html:
Each owner gets a yearly assessment notice in the mail, and the appeal clock runs 45 days from the day it is issued. Nothing is due on the notice. It lists the assessed value, the exemptions on file and your appeal rights. The last day for appeals and homestead applications is printed right on it, so go by that date.

Senate Bill 566 changed the statewide notice layout, so the older tax estimate tables gave way to an Estimated Tax Savings section.

  • Use the Property Search tool at augustarichmondtaxassessor.com, or deliver the appeal by post, email or in person.
  • Written appeals only, filed before day 45.
  • Direct questions to the Board of Assessors at 706-821-2310, and keep a copy of whatever you file.

Augusta grants a local floating homestead exemption for qualifying primary residences, limiting certain increases in assessed value. April 1 is the yearly filing date. Owners who file late receive a reduced share: 66.67% for April 2 through 30, 58.33% during May and 50% on June 1. Tax bills typically arrive in August or September.

Because the exemption belongs to the owner who applied, it does not simply carry over to a buyer. Ask the assessors what happens to it when title changes. Your buyer will want to know what the tax bill will look like after the sale.

Georgia taxes the transfer itself, using the sale price: $1 covers the first $1,000, then 10 cents for every further $100 or fraction of $100. The liability falls on the seller, though a contract may hand the cost to the buyer. The Richmond County clerk of superior court will hold the deed unrecorded until the tax is paid.

The reporting form is PT-61, filed through the clerks' online portal, and whoever handles your closing usually files it. Ask the tax commissioner what is owed on the current-year bill so the cost can be split between buyer and seller on the settlement statement. If a deed might qualify for an exemption, ask the county clerk of superior court. For filing problems, the portal's support line is 800-304-5174.

sections.h2: What to gather before you list
sections.html:
Having paperwork ready shortens any sale. Pull together your latest assessment notice, a record of the exemptions on file, any lease and rent ledger if tenants live there, and receipts or permits for past repairs. If the house sits in a historic district, add whatever approvals the preservation commission gave for earlier exterior work.

Then walk through the steps in order. Get your parcel's county value from the Board of Assessors, collect two or three written offers or a listing price opinion, pick a closing attorney, and ask the tax commissioner for the current bill so the proration is settled before closing day. A cash sale skips the appraisal, the lender's underwriting and the repair negotiation, which is why it can close on a date you set. A traditional sale takes on all three, and any one of them can move the closing date or the price.

sections.h2: When a quick as-is sale makes sense
sections.html:
Speed pays off when waiting costs more than the discount a cash buyer applies. The discount is real, so gather several offers and read each term.

  • An inherited Richmond County house that no relative wants to carry.
  • A rental with a lease in force, or repairs a lender's appraiser would flag.
  • A move pinned to a base or hospital start date.
  • A house with code violations or liens that complicate a regular listing.

Request proof of funds, an offer in writing and a fixed closing date from every buyer. The Board of Assessors can also tell you the county's value for your parcel, a useful benchmark before anyone names a price.

faqs.q: How many days does an Augusta owner have to contest an assessment?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the issue date on the notice. Online, postal, email and in-person filing are all accepted, and the office line is 706-821-2310.

faqs.q: Does Augusta have separate city and county governments?
faqs.a: No. Augusta and Richmond County became a single government in 1996, while Hephzibah and Blythe remain separate cities inside the county. Ask the tax commissioner what charges appear on your parcel's bill.

faqs.q: Who bears Georgia's transfer tax in an Augusta closing?
faqs.a: By default the seller, though the sales contract can move it to the buyer. Recording waits until it is paid.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Augusta house that has tenants or damage?
faqs.a: Often yes, since a cash buyer accepts the house as it is. A regular listing can close with tenants too, but loan-backed buyers tend to request repairs, so compare what you would net on each path.
About 202,000. The mid-2025 estimate is 201,999 for the consolidated government, and the 2020 census recorded 202,081.
